**File key** (base: `C:\Users\cable\Documents\dev\zig-parquet\.claude\worktrees\zig-parquet-perf-compat-dc9ccc\zig-parquet\src\`)
- `core\dynamic_reader.zig`, `core\parquet_reader.zig`, `core\column_decoder.zig`, `core\value.zig`, `core\nested.zig`, `core\page_range_reader.zig`, `core\safe.zig`, `core\seekable_reader.zig`
- `core\encoding\rle.zig`, `plain.zig`, `dictionary.zig`, `delta_binary_packed.zig`, `delta_length_byte_array.zig`, `delta_byte_array.zig`, `byte_stream_split.zig`
- `core\thrift\compact.zig`, `core\format\metadata.zig`, `column.zig`, `page.zig`, `statistics.zig`, `schema.zig`
- `core\compress\mod.zig`, `core\compress\snappy.zig`
- `io\file_reader.zig`, `io\buffer_reader.zig`, `api\zig\reader.zig`

Not analyzed in depth: `core\arrow_batch.zig` (it calls the same `readColumnChunkData` and decoders at lines 1097, 1168, 1238, 1729, so it probably shares these hotspots), `row_ranges.zig` (cost of `contains`), and the codec internals beyond snappy. `parquet_reader.zig` holds shared helpers only (footer, chunk read, `PageIterator`). `DynamicReader` does not use `PageIterator`; only tests and `reader_mod` reference it.

### 1. Bytes from file to page

- **Footer:** `parseFooter` (parquet_reader.zig:88-131) does three small reads: tail 8 bytes (:94), footer body (:110), head magic (:115). The footer buffer is kept alive for the reader's lifetime.
- **Column chunk, unfiltered:** `readColumnChunkData` (parquet_reader.zig:139-164) reads the entire chunk, from the dictionary page if present, in one `readAt` (:160) into one fresh allocation. `readColumnDynamicWithData` (dynamic_reader.zig:692) calls it at :706. Projection skips whole columns, but never individual pages.
- **Column chunk, filtered:** `readRowsFiltered` (dynamic_reader.zig:376-541) uses `readSelectedPages` (page_range_reader.zig:88-214). That is one allocation (:163), with contiguous selected pages coalesced into one `readAt` (:175-207). This is the good path.
- **Backends:** `FileReader.readAt` is one `readPositionalAll` per call with no buffering or readahead (file_reader.zig:36). `BufferReader` is a memcpy (buffer_reader.zig:40). Every read goes through a vtable (seekable_reader.zig:27-29).
- **Per-page copies:** the decompressed body is freshly allocated per page (dynamic_reader.zig:934-938 for V1, :877-889 for V2). Snappy allocates the full output and reallocs if the size differs (snappy.zig:59, :65). Uncompressed pages avoid the copy: the body is used as a slice (dynamic_reader.zig:937).
- **Headers:** when there is no dictionary, the first page header is parsed twice, once as a peek (dynamic_reader.zig:734-736) and again in the loop (:824-825).
- **Dictionary:** rebuilt per column chunk (dynamic_reader.zig:732-802). `StringDictionary.fromPlain` does one `allocator.dupe` per entry (dictionary.zig:36), and it is freed at the end of each chunk (:716-726).
- **CRC:** off by default (parquet_reader.zig:27). When enabled it runs over the compressed body (dynamic_reader.zig:844-853).

### 2. Value decoding

- **Dispatch:** per page, not per value. Encoding and physical type are switched once (column_decoder.zig:951-1011 for V1, :1015-1081 for V2).
- **PLAIN fixed-width:** `decodeRequiredColumn` (column_decoder.zig:716-853) uses `PlainDecoder` (plain.zig:86-130). Each value goes into a typed `Optional(T)` array first (allocated at column_decoder.zig:134), then is converted to `Value` in a second pass.
- **PLAIN with def levels:** `decodePlainWithDefLevels` (column_decoder.zig:641-713). For byte arrays it calls `isDecimalIntColumn` per value (:691) and does one `dupeBytes` per value (:701).
- **Dictionary:** `rle.decode` materializes all indices as a `u32` array per page (rle.zig:19-87). Then each value is looked up and, for strings, copied per row (column_decoder.zig:444, :752, :1540).
- **RLE / bit-packed:** the RLE run fills one `u32` at a time (rle.zig:73-76). Bit-packed unpacking (`decodeBitPacked`, rle.zig:150-179) runs per value: a division, a `castTo(u3)`, up to five byte loads each with a bounds check and a `castTo(u6)` (:166-170), then a 64-bit shift and mask. There is no bit-width specialization and no bulk unpack. `readVarInt` (:128-148) also uses `castTo` per byte.
- **Booleans:** `plain.decodeBool` does a `castTo(u3)` per value (plain.zig:21). The RLE boolean path builds a `u32` index array and then maps it.
- **DELTA_BINARY_PACKED:** the result is one allocation (delta_binary_packed.zig:81), but `unpackMiniBlock` (:198-243) does an 8-iteration byte loop per value with `castTo(u6)` (:224-226) and i128 arithmetic per value (:234-237). The column decoder then copies the result into a `Value` array (column_decoder.zig:2442-2519).
- **DELTA_LENGTH_BYTE_ARRAY:** one `allocator.dupe` per string (delta_length_byte_array.zig:56-63). The reader then dupes again through `dupeBytes` (column_decoder.zig:2559), so each string costs two allocations and two copies.
- **DELTA_BYTE_ARRAY:** one allocation per value plus a prefix memcpy (delta_byte_array.zig:108-113). A final copy into `const_result` (:131-135), then the reader's `dupeBytes` (column_decoder.zig:2614). That is two allocations per value, and the prefix bytes are copied again each time.
- **BYTE_STREAM_SPLIT:** the float/int variants allocate a typed array and then a `Value` array (column_decoder.zig:2656-2722). Fixed-length byte arrays allocate one slice per value (byte_stream_split.zig:149) and then dupe it again (column_decoder.zig:2762).
- **`@Vector`:** not used anywhere in `src`.
- **Inner-loop appends:** `readRowsFiltered` appends per value (dynamic_reader.zig:506-507). Nested assembly appends per element (nested.zig:420, :480, :500).

### 3. Row materialization

- **Shape:** `readRowsInternal` (dynamic_reader.zig:543-679) decodes every needed leaf column into a column-major `[]Value`, keeps the def/rep level arrays (:658-664), and then calls `assembleFlatRows` (:1112-1155).
- **Per-row cost:** `assembleFlatRows` allocates one `[]Value` per row (:1135) and deep-clones every cell with `cloneValue` (:1144). `cloneValue` dupes byte payloads again (dynamic_reader.zig:1196-1197).
- **Peak memory:** the column-major arrays stay alive until the `defer` at dynamic_reader.zig:632-638, so peak holds both copies.
- **Arena:** byte payloads go to `bytes_arena`, which is set at dynamic_reader.zig:553-555 and initialized at :119. Nothing calls `reset` on it. It is only freed in `deinit` (:175). `Row` is marked `bytes_borrowed`, so per-row frees skip payloads (value.zig:280-316). The `RowIterator` doc (dynamic_reader.zig:268-269) says it holds "at most one row group's worth of rows", but byte payloads for every row group already read stay live until the reader is closed.
- **Value size:** `Value` is a tagged union whose largest payload is a slice, so about 24 bytes per cell (value.zig:50-77).
- **Nested rows:** `assembleNestedRows` (dynamic_reader.zig:997-1110) builds per-row values in `assembleValues` (nested.zig:341-353). Struct field names are duped per row (nested.zig:499), and primitives are dupe-cloned (nested.zig:521-522). The result is cloned again (dynamic_reader.zig:1084, :1088). Nested byte values therefore see up to three copies. `SchemaNode.buildFromElements` also reruns per top-level column for every row group (dynamic_reader.zig:586-606).
- **Filtered mapping:** `mapDecodedRow` scans all selected pages linearly for every value (page_range_reader.zig:68-78). That is O(values × selected pages), used per value in dynamic_reader.zig:501.

### 4. Definition and repetition levels

- **V1 flat:** levels are length-prefixed RLE and are decoded into a `u32` array (column_decoder.zig:336-353, and `decodeLevelsForDynamicWithEncoding` at :1617-1704).
- **def_mask:** a second array of `bool` is built from those levels (column_decoder.zig:360-368, :1655, :1682-1686). So each page carries 5 bytes per value of level state.
- **Flat schemas keep them anyway:** the levels are stored (dynamic_reader.zig:662-663), appended into column-level lists (:923-927, :976-983), and freed without being read (:640-656). For flat tables, nothing uses them. `readRowsFiltered` frees them too (:485-487).
- **V2:** `decodeLevelsV2` (column_decoder.zig:1084-1131) skips the length prefix. It always allocates `def_mask` (:1104), even when `max_def_level` is 0.
- **Deprecated BIT_PACKED levels** go through the per-value unpacker (rle.zig:111-116).

### 5. Thrift metadata cost

- **Reader:** no allocation per field. `readFieldHeader` (compact.zig:129-153) and `skip` (:183-223) allocate nothing.
- **Varints:** byte at a time through `readByte` with error branches and a `std.math.cast(u6)` per byte (compact.zig:50-77). Cheap, but not vectorized.
- **Allocations:** only per list, string, and statistics value:
  - Per list: `metadata.zig:33`, `:42`, `:50`; `column.zig:43`; `row_group.zig:31`, `:41`.
  - Per string: `column.zig:53` (every `path_in_schema` entry), `schema.zig:43` (every element name), `metadata.zig:56` (`created_by`), `row_group.zig:156-157` (key/value metadata).
  - Per statistics: `statistics.zig:34-39` (min/max dupes, per column chunk and per page header that carries stats).
- **Error path:** `FileMetaData.parse` has no `errdefer` (metadata.zig:24-62), so a parse error partway through leaks everything allocated so far.

## Ranked hotspots

1. **Byte payloads are copied two or three times.** Decode dupes (column_decoder.zig:444, :701, :752, :1540, :1554, :2559, :2614, :2762) and then `cloneValue` dupes again (dynamic_reader.zig:1144 via :1196-1197; nested.zig:521-522). Transferring ownership of the decoded slices into the rows would remove one copy and one allocation per string.
2. **Row-major clone and a per-row allocation.** `assembleFlatRows` allocates `rows` slices and clones every cell (dynamic_reader.zig:1134-1152). That is N allocations plus N×C deep copies, and it doubles peak memory because column arrays stay alive (:632-638). Decoding straight into row-major storage, or using the column arrays as the storage for flat schemas, would remove both.
3. **The arena is never released across row groups.** Byte payloads accumulate until `DynamicReader.deinit` (dynamic_reader.zig:93, :119, :175, :553-555), which breaks the streaming doc at :268-269. A `RowIterator` over a large file grows memory roughly to the size of its decoded strings, times two. Releasing per-row-group payloads when the rows are freed would fix it.
4. **Three full-size arrays per page.** The typed `Optional(T)` array (column_decoder.zig:134), then a `Value` array (for example :1829-1835), then `appendSlice` into the column (dynamic_reader.zig:917, :971). Decoding directly into a column-level `Value` buffer sized from the chunk's `num_values` would cut this to one.
5. **Levels are built for flat columns that never use them.** The `u32` levels, the `bool` mask, and the copies into column lists (column_decoder.zig:336-368, :1604-1704; dynamic_reader.zig:640-663, :923-927, :976-983) are all discarded for flat schemas. Skipping level materialization when `max_def_level` is 0, and using a bitmap when it is 1, removes most of this.
6. **Per-value RLE/bit-packed unpacking, and dictionary indices materialized as `u32`.** `decodeBitPacked` (rle.zig:150-179) and the RLE fill (:73-76) dominate dictionary columns, which are the most common case for strings and low-cardinality ints. A specialized unpacker per bit width (an 8-byte load, shift, and mask per value) and decoding indices straight into the consumer would help most.
7. **Unfiltered reads hold the whole chunk and allocate per page.** `readColumnChunkData` (parquet_reader.zig:139-164) reads the whole chunk, and each page allocates its decompressed buffer (dynamic_reader.zig:934-938, :877-889; snappy.zig:59). Reusing one scratch buffer per column, or streaming pages, cuts allocations and peak memory.
8. **Delta and BYTE_STREAM_SPLIT allocate per value.** Delta unpacking uses an 8-byte loop and i128 math per value (delta_binary_packed.zig:223-237). Delta-length and delta-byte-array allocate per string and then dupe again (delta_length_byte_array.zig:60; delta_byte_array.zig:108, :131-135; column_decoder.zig:2559, :2614). FLBA byte-stream-split allocates per value (byte_stream_split.zig:149). Decoding into one contiguous buffer with an offsets array would remove most allocations.
9. **Filtered reads scan selected pages per value.** `mapDecodedRow` (page_range_reader.zig:68-78) is linear per value, and `kept_values` / `kept_indices` append per value (dynamic_reader.zig:506-507). A running cursor over the selected pages, with reserved capacity, makes this linear.
10. **Footer and per-chunk repeated work.** Per-chunk and per-element allocations (metadata.zig:33-50; column.zig:43-53; schema.zig:43; statistics.zig:34-39). Also the first page header is parsed twice (dynamic_reader.zig:734-736 and :825), dictionaries are rebuilt per chunk (:732-802), `getColumnInfo` runs per chunk (:768, :805), and the schema tree is rebuilt per row group (:586-606). The cost scales with columns × row groups, so it matters for wide or many-row-group files more than for big single-column scans.

**Latent hazards (not live today):**
- `decodeColumnWithLevelsAndDeltaEncoding` (column_decoder.zig:156-218) frees arena-owned payloads with `ctx.allocator` (:183-184, :200). It is currently unreachable because no `DecodeContext` sets `value_encoding`.
- `FileMetaData.parse` leaks on error (see section 5).

**Suggested next step:** measure allocation counts with a counting allocator on a string-heavy file. The comment at value.zig:20-22 mentions about 440k allocations on `covid.snappy.parquet`, which gives a baseline to check the first three items against.

## READ path map: DynamicReader to bytes (zig-parquet)

Static read-only analysis; nothing was built or run, so the performance claims are from source, not profiling. All line numbers are in the files below.

**File key** (base: `C:\Users\cable\Documents\dev\zig-parquet\.claude\worktrees\zig-parquet-perf-compat-dc9ccc\zig-parquet\src\`)
- `core\dynamic_reader.zig`, `core\parquet_reader.zig`, `core\column_decoder.zig`, `core\value.zig`, `core\nested.zig`, `core\page_range_reader.zig`, `core\safe.zig`, `core\seekable_reader.zig`
- `core\encoding\rle.zig`, `plain.zig`, `dictionary.zig`, `delta_binary_packed.zig`, `delta_length_byte_array.zig`, `delta_byte_array.zig`, `byte_stream_split.zig`
- `core\thrift\compact.zig`, `core\format\metadata.zig`, `column.zig`, `page.zig`, `statistics.zig`, `schema.zig`
- `core\compress\mod.zig`, `core\compress\snappy.zig`
- `io\file_reader.zig`, `io\buffer_reader.zig`, `api\zig\reader.zig`

Not analyzed in depth: `core\arrow_batch.zig` (calls the same `readColumnChunkData` and decoders at lines 1097, 1168, 1238, 1729, so it probably shares these hotspots), `row_ranges.zig` (cost of `contains`), and codec internals beyond snappy. `parquet_reader.zig` holds shared helpers only (footer, chunk read, `PageIterator`). `DynamicReader` does not use `PageIterator`.

### 1. Bytes from file to page
- **Footer:** `parseFooter` (parquet_reader.zig:88-131) does three small reads: tail 8 bytes (:94), footer body (:110), head magic (:115). The footer buffer stays alive for the reader's lifetime.
- **Column chunk, unfiltered:** `readColumnChunkData` (parquet_reader.zig:139-164) reads the whole chunk, from the dictionary page if present, in one `readAt` (:160) into one fresh allocation. Called via dynamic_reader.zig:706 and :1158. Projection skips whole columns, never individual pages.
- **Column chunk, filtered:** `readRowsFiltered` (dynamic_reader.zig:376-541) uses `readSelectedPages` (page_range_reader.zig:88-214): one allocation (:163), contiguous selected pages coalesced into one `readAt` (:175-207). This is the good path.
- **Backends:** `FileReader.readAt` is one `readPositionalAll` per call, no buffering or readahead (file_reader.zig:36). `BufferReader` is a memcpy (buffer_reader.zig:40). Every read goes through a vtable (seekable_reader.zig:27-29).
- **Per-page copies:** decompressed body is freshly allocated per page (dynamic_reader.zig:934-938 V1, :877-889 V2). Snappy allocates full output and reallocs on size mismatch (snappy.zig:59, :65). Uncompressed pages avoid the copy (body used as slice, dynamic_reader.zig:937).
- **Headers:** with no dictionary, the first page header is parsed twice: peek (dynamic_reader.zig:734-736), then again in the loop (:824-825).
- **Dictionary:** rebuilt per column chunk (dynamic_reader.zig:732-802). `StringDictionary.fromPlain` does one `allocator.dupe` per entry (dictionary.zig:36), freed at chunk end (:716-726).
- **CRC:** off by default (parquet_reader.zig:27). When on, computed over compressed body (dynamic_reader.zig:844-853).

### 2. Value decoding
- **Dispatch:** per page, not per value. Encoding and physical type switched once (column_decoder.zig:951-1011 V1, :1015-1081 V2).
- **PLAIN fixed-width:** `decodeRequiredColumn` (column_decoder.zig:716-853) uses `PlainDecoder` (plain.zig:86-130). Values go into a typed `Optional(T)` array first (allocated at column_decoder.zig:134), then converted to `Value` in a second pass.
- **PLAIN with def levels:** `decodePlainWithDefLevels` (column_decoder.zig:641-713). For byte arrays, calls `isDecimalIntColumn` per value (:691) and one `dupeBytes` per value (:701).
- **Dictionary:** `rle.decode` materializes all indices as a `u32` array per page (rle.zig:19-87). Each value is looked up and, for strings, copied per row (column_decoder.zig:444, :752, :1540).
- **RLE / bit-packed:** RLE run fills one `u32` at a time (rle.zig:73-76). `decodeBitPacked` (rle.zig:150-179) runs per value: a division, `castTo(u3)`, up to five byte loads each with a bounds check and `castTo(u6)` (:166-170), then 64-bit shift and mask. No bit-width specialization, no bulk unpack. `readVarInt` (:128-148) also uses `castTo` per byte.
- **Booleans:** `plain.decodeBool` does `castTo(u3)` per value (plain.zig:21). RLE boolean path builds a `u32` index array then maps it.
- **DELTA_BINARY_PACKED:** result is one allocation (delta_binary_packed.zig:81), but `unpackMiniBlock` (:198-243) does an 8-iteration byte loop per value with `castTo(u6)` (:224-226) and i128 arithmetic per value (:234-237). Column decoder copies into a `Value` array (column_decoder.zig:2442-2519).
- **DELTA_LENGTH_BYTE_ARRAY:** one `allocator.dupe` per string (delta_length_byte_array.zig:56-63), then `dupeBytes` again (column_decoder.zig:2559): two allocations and two copies per string.
- **DELTA_BYTE_ARRAY:** one allocation per value plus prefix memcpy (delta_byte_array.zig:108-113), final copy into `const_result` (:131-135), then `dupeBytes` (column_decoder.zig:2614). Two allocations per value; prefix bytes copied again each time.
- **BYTE_STREAM_SPLIT:** float/int variants allocate a typed array then a `Value` array (column_decoder.zig:2656-2722). FLBA allocates one slice per value (byte_stream_split.zig:149), then dupes again (column_decoder.zig:2762).
- **`@Vector`:** not used anywhere in `src` (grep: no matches).
- **Inner-loop appends:** `readRowsFiltered` appends per value (dynamic_reader.zig:506-507). Nested assembly appends per element (nested.zig:420, :480, :500).

### 3. Row materialization
- **Shape:** `readRowsInternal` (dynamic_reader.zig:543-679) decodes every needed leaf into a column-major `[]Value`, keeps def/rep level arrays (:658-664), then `assembleFlatRows` (:1112-1155).
- **Per-row cost:** `assembleFlatRows` allocates one `[]Value` per row (:1135) and deep-clones each cell via `cloneValue` (:1144). `cloneValue` dupes byte payloads again (dynamic_reader.zig:1196-1197).
- **Peak memory:** column-major arrays stay alive until the defer at dynamic_reader.zig:632-638, so peak holds both copies.
- **Arena:** byte payloads go to `bytes_arena`, set at dynamic_reader.zig:553-555, initialized at :119, freed only in `deinit` (:175). Nothing calls `reset` on it. `Row` is `bytes_borrowed`, so per-row frees skip payloads (value.zig:280-316). The `RowIterator` doc (dynamic_reader.zig:268-269) says it holds "at most one row group's worth of rows", but byte payloads for every row group already read remain live until the reader is closed.
- **Value size:** `Value` union's largest payload is a slice, so about 24 bytes per cell (value.zig:50-77).
- **Nested rows:** `assembleNestedRows` (dynamic_reader.zig:997-1110) builds per-row values in `assembleValues` (nested.zig:341-353). Struct field names duped per row (nested.zig:499); primitives dupe-cloned (nested.zig:521-522); result cloned again (dynamic_reader.zig:1084, :1088). Nested byte values see up to three copies. `SchemaNode.buildFromElements` reruns per top-level column for each row group (dynamic_reader.zig:586-606).
- **Filtered mapping:** `mapDecodedRow` scans all selected pages linearly for every value (page_range_reader.zig:68-78), used per value at dynamic_reader.zig:501. O(values x selected pages).

### 4. Definition and repetition levels
- **V1 flat:** length-prefixed RLE decoded to a `u32` array (column_decoder.zig:336-353; `decodeLevelsForDynamicWithEncoding` at :1617-1704).
- **def_mask:** a second `bool` array built from those levels (column_decoder.zig:360-368, :1655, :1682-1686). About 5 bytes of level state per value per page.
- **Flat schemas keep them anyway:** stored (dynamic_reader.zig:662-663), appended into column-level lists (:923-927, :976-983), then freed unread (:640-656). For flat tables nothing uses them. `readRowsFiltered` frees them too (:485-487).
- **V2:** `decodeLevelsV2` (column_decoder.zig:1084-1131) skips the length prefix but always allocates `def_mask` (:1104), even with `max_def_level` 0.
- **BIT_PACKED levels** go through the per-value unpacker (rle.zig:111-116).

### 5. Thrift metadata cost
- **Reader:** no allocation per field. `readFieldHeader` (compact.zig:129-153) and `skip` (:183-223) allocate nothing.
- **Varints:** byte-at-a-time via `readByte` with error branches and `std.math.cast(u6)` per byte (compact.zig:50-77).
- **Allocations** only per list, string, and statistics value:
  - Per list: metadata.zig:33, :42, :50; column.zig:43; row_group.zig:31, :41.
  - Per string: column.zig:53 (every `path_in_schema` entry), schema.zig:43 (every element name), metadata.zig:56 (`created_by`), row_group.zig:156-157 (KV).
  - Per statistics: statistics.zig:34-39 (min/max dupes, per column chunk and per page header carrying stats).
- **Error path:** `FileMetaData.parse` has no `errdefer` (metadata.zig:24-62), so a mid-parse error leaks everything allocated so far.

## Ranked hotspots
1. **Byte payloads copied two or three times.** Decode dupes (column_decoder.zig:444, :701, :752, :1540, :1554, :2559, :2614, :2762) then `cloneValue` dupes again (dynamic_reader.zig:1144 via :1196-1197; nested.zig:521-522). Transferring ownership of decoded slices into rows removes one copy and one allocation per string.
2. **Row-major clone and per-row allocation.** `assembleFlatRows` allocates a slice per row and clones every cell (dynamic_reader.zig:1134-1152): N allocations plus N x C deep copies, and column arrays stay alive (:632-638) so peak doubles. Decoding into row-major storage, or using column arrays as row storage for flat schemas, removes both.
3. **Arena never released across row groups.** Payloads accumulate until `DynamicReader.deinit` (dynamic_reader.zig:93, :119, :175, :553-555), breaking the streaming doc at :268-269. A `RowIterator` over a large file grows memory to roughly the decoded string size times two. Releasing per-row-group payloads when rows are freed would fix it.
4. **Three full-size arrays per page.** Typed `Optional(T)` (column_decoder.zig:134), then `Value` (for example :1829-1835), then `appendSlice` into the column (dynamic_reader.zig:917, :971). Decoding directly into a column-level `Value` buffer sized from chunk `num_values` cuts it to one.
5. **Levels built for flat columns that never use them.** `u32` levels, `bool` mask, and copies into column lists (column_decoder.zig:336-368, :1604-1704; dynamic_reader.zig:640-663, :923-927, :976-983) are discarded for flat schemas. Skipping levels when `max_def_level` is 0 and using a bitmap when 1 removes most of it.
6. **Per-value RLE/bit-packed unpacking; dictionary indices materialized as `u32`.** `decodeBitPacked` (rle.zig:150-179) and the RLE fill (:73-76) dominate dictionary columns, the most common case for strings and low-cardinality ints. A bit-width-specialized unpacker and decoding indices straight into the consumer would help most.
7. **Unfiltered reads hold the whole chunk and allocate per page.** `readColumnChunkData` (parquet_reader.zig:139-164) reads the whole chunk, and each page allocates its decompressed buffer (dynamic_reader.zig:934-938, :877-889; snappy.zig:59). A reusable scratch buffer per column, or streaming pages, cuts allocations and peak memory.
8. **Delta and BYTE_STREAM_SPLIT allocate per value.** Delta unpacking uses an 8-byte loop and i128 math per value (delta_binary_packed.zig:223-237). Delta-length and delta-byte-array allocate per string then dupe again (delta_length_byte_array.zig:60; delta_byte_array.zig:108, :131-135; column_decoder.zig:2559, :2614). FLBA byte-stream-split allocates per value (byte_stream_split.zig:149). One contiguous buffer plus offsets would remove most allocations.
9. **Filtered reads scan selected pages per value.** `mapDecodedRow` (page_range_reader.zig:68-78) is linear per value; `kept_values` / `kept_indices` append per value (dynamic_reader.zig:506-507). A running cursor over selected pages, with reserved capacity, makes this linear.
10. **Footer and per-chunk repeated work.** Per-chunk and per-element allocations (metadata.zig:33-50; column.zig:43-53; schema.zig:43; statistics.zig:34-39). First page header parsed twice (dynamic_reader.zig:734-736 and :825); dictionaries rebuilt per chunk (:732-802); `getColumnInfo` per chunk (:768, :805); schema tree rebuilt per row group (:586-606). Cost scales with columns x row groups: matters for wide or many-row-group files more than big single-column scans.

**Latent hazards (not live today):**
- `decodeColumnWithLevelsAndDeltaEncoding` (column_decoder.zig:156-218) frees arena-owned payloads with `ctx.allocator` (:183-184, :200). Unreachable now: no `DecodeContext` sets `value_encoding`.
- `FileMetaData.parse` leaks on error (section 5).

**Suggested next step:** measure allocation counts with a counting allocator on a string-heavy file. The comment at value.zig:20-22 cites about 440k allocations on `covid.snappy.parquet`, a baseline for checking items 1-3.
